rounds.text: Hisar Metal Industries Ltd trades at a modest P/E of 16.2x and a price-to-book ratio of 1.17x, both of which sit at attractive discounts compared to sector benchmarks of 22.49x and 2.44x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. The company is showing powerful fundamental acceleration, evidenced by a 74% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a dramatic surge in quarterly operating margins to 7% in June 2026 compared to 4% in the year-ago quarter [E21, E31]. Furthermore, cash generation is exceptionally strong with a cash conversion of 3.67x against reported profit, yielding Rs 11 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 6 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E34, E35, E36]. Operational capacity expansion is near completion as capital work-in-progress dropped 66.7% over the prior year, positioning the business to capitalise on a supportive Capital Goods sector tailwind [E40, E71]. Conceded: debt-to-equity is elevated at 1.34x with borrowings reaching Rs 87 Cr, long-term sales growth has been modest at 4% over ten years, and a discounted cash flow model suggests the current price of Rs 143 sits above intrinsic value [E14, E38, E39, E44].

Hisar Metal Industries Ltd carries a significant valuation disconnect, trading at ₹ 143 per share against a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of only ₹ 102 per share, which leaves a negative margin of safety of 40.4% [E44, E45]. The fundamental profitability metrics flag severe structural weaknesses, featuring a low return on equity of 5.0% and return on capital employed of 7.5%, both lagging far behind their respective sector benchmarks of 10.84% and 12.92% [E9, E10, E13]. Furthermore, the balance sheet carries real vulnerability as debt to equity sits at 1.34x with total borrowings escalating to ₹ 87 Cr in March 2026, compounded by low interest coverage and an overall rules-based screen score of 54 out of 100 pointing to a SELL with low confidence [E38, E39, E59, E62]. Compounded profit growth over 3 years and 5 years stands in negative territory at -34% and -10% respectively, while compounded 3-year sales growth has contracted by -2% [E16, E19, E20]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing momentum with a TTM profit growth of 74%, a June 2026 quarterly profit surge of 329% YoY, robust cash conversion of 3.67x, and operates within a Capital Goods sector tailwind [E21, E31, E34, E64, E73].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model suggests a valuation of ₹ 102 against the current price of ₹ 143, and historical 3-year and 5-year profit growth figures are indeed negative [E19, E20, E44]. However, the bear overlooks that the company is currently experiencing a powerful operational turnaround led by a massive 74% trailing twelve-month profit growth and a 329% year-on-year profit surge in the June 2026 quarter [E21, E64]. Furthermore, quarterly operating margins have expanded by 3 percentage points to 7% in June 2026 compared to the same period a year ago, reflecting accelerating momentum that stale historical averages fail to capture [E31, E72]. Conceded: debt-to-equity is elevated at 1.34x and capital efficiency ratios lag sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E38]. Yet, capital expenditure is largely complete with capital work-in-progress dropping by 66.7%, and operating cash flow stands at a robust ₹ 11 Cr with a high cash conversion ratio of 3.67x ensuring profits are fully backed by actual cash [E34, E35, E40]. Finally, the business benefits from operating squarely inside a supportive Capital Goods sector tailwind that provides a strong macro backdrop for this emerging improvement [E71].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 74% and net profit surged 329% year-on-year in the June 2026 quarter [E21, E64]. However, relying on these short-term metrics ignores the longer-term structural reality where 5-year profit growth is -10% and 3-year profit growth is -34% [E19, E20]. Conceded: quarterly operating margins expanded by 3 percentage points to 7% in June 2026 [E31]. Yet, the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are officially categorized as inconsistent over the last two years and two quarters, meaning this expansion lacks durability [E32, E33]. Conceded: operating cash flow reached ₹ 11 Cr with a high cash conversion of 3.67x [E34, E35]. Nevertheless, borrowings simultaneously expanded from ₹ 70 Cr to ₹ 87 Cr, pushing debt-to-equity to an elevated 1.34x where debt exceeds net worth and interest coverage is low [E38, E39, E59]. Finally, while sector tailwinds are present [E71], the company's internal return on equity of 5.14% and return on capital employed of 7.5% severely underperform sector benchmarks of 10.84% and 12.92%, leaving a substantial -40.4% discount to its discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 102 [E9, E10, E44, E45].
